title: The seven PRINCE2 principles
blurb: Recall the seven principles by their Version 2 names, say what each requires and explain why principles are never tailored away.
question: The project board authorizes one stage at a time and lets the project manager control each stage day to day within agreed tolerances. Which principle is this?

teach.body: The principles are the guiding obligations and good practices that decide whether a project is genuinely being managed with PRINCE2. All seven must be applied. What you tailor is how they are applied, not whether: dropping a principle means the project is no longer PRINCE2. PRINCE2 Agile uses the same seven principles as PRINCE2 Project Management.

teach.h: The seven principles and what each requires
head: Principle
What it requires
rows: A valid reason for the project that stays valid throughout
Seek, record and use lessons before, during and after
Right people, clear roles, stakeholders engaged
Plan, monitor and control stage by stage
Delegate within tolerances for seven aspects
Deliver well-defined outputs, not just activities
Adapt to size, complexity, risk and context
teach.caption: Names as in the V2 book 5.2; requirements paraphrased from 5.2.1.1 to 5.2.1.7.

teach.body: Ensure continued business justification: the project needs a valid justification that stays relevant throughout its life; without it, projects drift on with few benefits or poor strategic fit. Manage by stages: the project is planned, monitored and controlled stage by stage; the board authorizes one stage at a time and delegates day-to-day control within tolerances to the project manager.

Manage by exception: governance by delegating responsibilities and setting tolerances for benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. Focus on products: deliver well-defined outputs, which avoids unnecessary work, prevents scope creep, sets clear expectations and allows a controlled close or pause. Tailor to suit the project: adapt to its size, complexity, risk and organizational context.

teach.h: Manage by stages versus manage by exception

children.label: Must be applied
children.sub: how it is applied can adapt

teach.h: Spot the principle from the clue

teach.body: At Ashworth Engineering, a new parts-tracking system is under way. Executive Helen Marsh checks the business case at each stage boundary (continued business justification). The team reviews lessons from a previous rollout (learn from experience). The board authorizes stage two only (manage by stages) and sets the stage tolerances within which project manager Daniel Osei may act (manage by exception). Each release delivers defined products (focus on products), and reporting is kept light for a small team (tailor).

teach.text: Watch the Version 2 names: 'ensure continued business justification' (not just 'continued business justification') and 'tailor to suit the project' (not 'project environment'). And principles are not optional: tailoring changes how a principle is applied, never whether it is applied.

items: Seven principles: ensure continued business justification, learn from experience, define roles, responsibilities and relationships, manage by stages, manage by exception, focus on products, tailor to suit the project.
All seven must be applied; their application is tailored, not the principles themselves.
Manage by stages: the board authorizes one stage at a time.
Manage by exception: tolerances for the seven performance aspects.

summary: You can now name all seven principles with their Version 2 wording and say what each one requires. You can also tell close pairs apart, such as manage by stages and manage by exception.

A.q: Which principle requires a project to have a valid justification that stays relevant throughout its lifecycle?
A.why: A valid justification that remains relevant throughout the lifecycle is 'ensure continued business justification' (5.2.1.1).

whyNot.1: Tailoring adapts the method to size, complexity, risk and context.
whyNot.2: Manage by exception sets tolerances for the seven aspects.
whyNot.3: Defining roles is about the right people with clear roles and engaged stakeholders.

A.q: The project board authorizes one stage at a time and delegates day-to-day control within tolerances to the project manager. Which principle is this?
A.why: Planning, monitoring and controlling stage by stage, with the board authorizing one stage at a time, is 'manage by stages' (5.2.1.4).

whyNot.0: Manage by exception is about setting tolerances for the seven aspects; the stage-by-stage authorization is the key here.
whyNot.1: Focus on products is about well-defined outputs.
whyNot.3: Defining roles is about the right people with clear responsibilities.

A.q: Which principle says PRINCE2 should be adapted to the project's size, complexity, risk and organizational context?
A.why: 'Tailor to suit the project' adapts PRINCE2 to size, complexity, risk and organizational context (5.2.1.7).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience is about seeking and using lessons.
whyNot.1: Manage by stages is about stage-by-stage control.
whyNot.2: This principle is about valid justification throughout.

B.q: Which principle establishes governance by delegating responsibilities and setting tolerances for benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk?
B.why: Setting tolerances for the seven performance aspects is 'manage by exception' (5.2.1.5).

whyNot.0: Manage by stages is about authorizing one stage at a time.
whyNot.2: Focus on products is about delivering well-defined outputs.
whyNot.3: This principle is about the project staying justified.

B.q: A team agrees clear descriptions of each deliverable so that no unnecessary work is done and scope creep is avoided. Which principle is being applied?
B.why: Focus on products emphasizes well-defined outputs; its benefits include avoiding unnecessary work and preventing scope creep (5.2.1.6).

whyNot.0: Manage by exception concerns tolerances and escalation.
whyNot.3: Tailoring concerns adapting the method to the project.

B.q: A sponsor proposes dropping 'manage by stages' because the project is small. What is the correct response in PRINCE2?
options: Agree, because small projects may omit principles
Agree, if the board records it in the project log
Keep it, and add extra stages to compensate
Keep it, but apply it in a lighter, tailored way
B.why: All seven principles must be applied; tailoring changes how they are applied (for example fewer, larger stages), not whether.

whyNot.0: Principles are not omitted for any project size; that is what tailoring is for.
whyNot.1: Recording a decision does not make dropping a principle acceptable.
whyNot.2: Adding stages is the opposite of what a small project needs; tailor the application instead.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. 'Learn from experience' means seeking, recording and using lessons throughout the project.
2. A project can drop one principle if it is tailored heavily.
3. 'Define roles, responsibilities and relationships' includes engaging internal and external stakeholders.
4. 'Manage by exception' means the board authorizes one stage at a time.
C.why: Statement 1 describes learn from experience; statement 3 describes define roles, responsibilities and relationships (5.2.1.3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: all seven principles must be applied.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: principles are not dropped, and one stage at a time is manage by stages.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: that describes manage by stages.

C.q: Which list gives two principles using their Version 2 names?
options: Ensure continued business justification; tailor to suit the project
Continued business justification; tailor to suit the project environment
Defined roles and responsibilities; continued business justification
Learn from experience; tailor to suit the project environment
C.why: Version 2 uses 'ensure continued business justification' and 'tailor to suit the project' (5.2).

whyNot.1: Both names are the older (6th edition and Agile V1) wording.
whyNot.2: Both are older names; V2 adds 'ensure' and 'relationships'.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience is current, but 'project environment' is the older tailoring name.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Under 'manage by stages', the project board authorizes one stage at a time and delegates day-to-day control of the stage to the [?] within agreed tolerances.
C.why: The board delegates day-to-day control of the stage to the project manager within agreed tolerances (5.2.1.4).

whyNot.0: The product owner manages one team's product backlog, not the stage.
whyNot.2: The agile coach supports agile adoption across the organization.
whyNot.3: Project assurance monitors independently for the board; it does not control the stage.

reteach.title: A sentence for each principle
reteach.question: How can you remember all seven principles quickly?

items: Is it still worth doing? Ensure continued business justification.
What did we learn last time? Learn from experience.
Who does what, and with whom? Define roles, responsibilities and relationships.
One chunk at a time. Manage by stages.
Tell me only if limits will be broken. Manage by exception.
What exactly are we delivering? Focus on products.
Fit the method to the job. Tailor to suit the project.

blocks.text: Tailoring applies to how a principle is used. It never removes one.

explain.body: Ensure continued business justification: a valid reason for the project that remains relevant throughout. Without it, projects proceed with minimal benefit or poor strategic fit (5.2.1.1).

test.q: What risk does the 'ensure continued business justification' principle guard against?
options: Teams changing their chosen delivery framework
Projects carrying on with poor strategic fit
Stages running longer than first planned
Roles being shared between several people
test.why: Without rigorous justification, projects may proceed with minimal benefits or poor strategic fit (5.2.1.1).

whyNot.0: Choice of delivery framework is a tailoring matter.
whyNot.2: Stage length is a manage by stages and planning matter.
whyNot.3: Shared roles are covered by the people and organization guidance.

explain.body: Manage by stages: one stage at a time. Manage by exception: tolerances for seven aspects, escalate only when they are forecast to be exceeded.

test.q: Tolerances are set for the seven performance aspects so the board need only step in when they are forecast to be exceeded. Which principle is this?
test.why: Setting tolerances for the seven aspects is manage by exception (5.2.1.5).

whyNot.1: Manage by stages is about authorizing one stage at a time.
whyNot.2: Focus on products is about well-defined outputs.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience is about lessons.

explain.body: Deliver well-defined outputs rather than only activities. Benefits: less unnecessary work, no uncontrolled scope creep, clear expectations, controlled closure or pause (5.2.1.6).

test.q: Which is a benefit of the 'focus on products' principle?
options: It removes the need for stage boundaries
It lets the board skip tolerance setting
It helps prevent uncontrolled scope creep
It replaces the business case with outputs
test.why: Focusing on well-defined products helps prevent uncontrolled changes (scope creep) (5.2.1.6).

whyNot.0: Stage boundaries belong to manage by stages and stay in place.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are still set under manage by exception.
whyNot.3: Business justification is still needed; products serve the business case.

explain.body: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships: right people, clear roles, stakeholders engaged (5.2.1.3). Learn from experience: lessons sought, recorded and applied throughout.

test.q: A project manager makes sure internal and external stakeholders are identified and engaged and that everyone knows their role. Which principle is this?
test.why: Clear roles and engaged internal and external stakeholders are 'define roles, responsibilities and relationships' (5.2.1.3).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience is about lessons.
whyNot.1: Tailoring is about adapting the method.
whyNot.2: This principle is about the project staying justified throughout.
